title: Risotto con Scampi
subtitle: Langoustine risotto with white wine and tomato
excerpt: Risotto con scampi is a Venetian luxury: risotto made with langoustine tails, their shells used to make a fragrant bisque. The result is sweeter and more delicate than prawn risotto. It is the risotto served in the best Venetian fish restaurants along the Rialto market and on the Giudecca.
sourceNotes: Scampi (langoustines) are central to Venetian seafood cooking. The Rialto fish market in Venice has sold langoustines from the northern Adriatic for centuries. Risotto con scampi is the prestige seafood risotto of the Veneto region.

content.text: Langoustine tails are sweet and tender but cook in seconds -- they are the very last thing to go into the risotto. The shells and any heads make an excellent stock in 20 minutes. If buying whole langoustines, reserve the shells. If buying ready-prepared tails, use a light fish stock or diluted chicken stock instead.

Fry the reserved langoustine shells in a little olive oil for 3 minutes until pink and fragrant. Add {{tomato}} tomato, crush briefly, then add 1.2 litres of water. Simmer for 20 minutes. Strain and keep hot.
Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed. Add the hot langoustine stock a ladleful at a time, stirring for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente. Season with {{salt-table}} salt.
Add {{langoustine-tails}} langoustine tails and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until just opaque and pink. Stir in {{parsley-flat}} parsley and serve at once.

items.cause: Overcooked -- they only need 90 seconds to 2 minutes.
items.fix: Add langoustines only when the rice is completely done and the pan is off the heat, or just about to come off. Residual heat from the risotto is enough to cook them.

content.text: Langoustines (scampi in Italian) are fished in the northern Adriatic and are one of the prize catches at the Rialto fish market in Venice. Risotto con scampi is considered the most elegant of the Venetian seafood risotti. It does not use Parmesan -- in Venetian and Italian coastal cooking generally, cheese is not added to seafood dishes.
